IFR reports five million industrial robots operating worldwide

World Robotics 2026 puts 2025 installations above 600,000, with China accounting for 59% and the United States becoming the second-largest market.

The Robot Report ↗24 September 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 4

Installed stock and annual additions differ

IFR’s World Robotics 2026 report puts operational industrial-robot stock in 2025 at about five million, up 9%. New installations during that year exceeded 600,000, up 11%. These measure different things and should not be used interchangeably.

Asia’s markets moved in different directions

China installed about 354,000 robots, up 20%, representing 59% of global additions. Japan installed 36,219, down 19%; South Korea about 30,000, down 1%; and India nearly 10,500, up 15%. Growth was not uniform across the region.

The US moves into second place

US installations rose 12% to nearly 38,500, overtaking Japan to become the second-largest market after China. Germany remained Europe’s largest market, but additions fell 8% to fewer than 25,000. Italy, France and Spain also declined.

Forecasts are not completed installations

IFR forecasts 655,000 installations in 2026 and 806,000 in 2029, with labor shortages and supply-chain changes supporting demand. Those figures are projections rather than already recorded deployments.
